newsitem.title: UK: Geoffrey Rippon, UK's EC negotiator, dead at 72.
newsitem.headline: Geoffrey Rippon, UK's EC negotiator, dead at 72.

text.p: Lord Rippon, who negotiated Britain's successful entry into the European Community, has died after a long illness. He was 72.
His death on Tuesday at his home in western England was announced by Unichem, the drugs firm of which he was chairman.

Rippon, a skilled lawyer who held several government posts under three prime ministers, including environment and technology, was given the job of handling the EC membership talks by then prime minister Edward Heath in 1970.
Heath said Rippon, by winning the trust of the rest of the Community, had played a crucial role in paving the way for Britain's entry into the bloc in 1973.

"He was skilful in handling not only international affairs but also domestic problems, and his ability to influence not only members of both houses of parliament but also the press and the public was of immense value," Heath said in a statement.
"He is a great loss to the Conservative Party," Heath added.
He was ennobled as Lord Rippon of Hexham in 1987 and is survived by his wife and four children.
